A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Prioritized Generative Replay (PGR) work. Their text, equations, figures, and tables are readable. v1 ends with references; v2 retains the main study and adds Appendices A–D.

before.justification: v1 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments on DMC and OpenAI Gym, including performance, generation diagnostics, and scaling studies in Section 5.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and reports additional experiments involving alternative relevance functions, DMLab navigation, exploration methods, corrupted observations, and alternative generators.

M1.justification: Although Algorithm 1 is retained, v2 substantially expands its concrete implementations: RND-, pseudo-count-, and episodic-curiosity relevance functions; a PPO-backed adaptation; combinations with noisy and bootstrapped Q-networks; and a conditional VAE generator. These change components and procedures in the added variants, rather than merely explaining the original implementation.

E1.justification: v2 adds DMLab Sparse/Very Sparse maze navigation with stochastic pixel distractors, state-based DMC Walker-Walk and Hopper-Hop evaluations, and Hopper-Stand sensitivity experiments. Appendix C also introduces corrupted training-observation scenarios. These substantially extend v1's DMC/OpenAI Gym control coverage.

E2.justification: Added comparators include PPO with ICM/RND/ECO bonuses, REDQ-based NoisyNets and Boot-DQN, MAX, and an unconditional VAE. Table 9 also adds PER comparisons on Reacher-Hard, beyond the Cheetah-Run and Quadruped-Walk comparisons in v1's Figure 3a. The original main-table comparators remain.

E3.justification: The retained main experiments keep their settings, but new protocols include 10M-step DMLab training with noisy image quadrants, corruption of 20% of dynamics-training transitions, MAX adapted to REDQ, generator substitutions, and an inner-loop-frequency sweep. Appendix C describes state noise, whereas Table 8's caption says action noise, leaving that detail inconsistent.

E4.justification: Appendices A–D add tests of alternative curiosity signals, noisy-TV robustness, compatibility with implicit exploration methods, sensitivity to corrupted dynamics training, diffusion versus VAE generation, and generative-buffer refresh frequency. These address substantial new questions; the explicit-bonus comparison and some PER results instead repeat analyses already present in v1.

E5.justification: v2 newly specifies three seeds for the explicit-exploration comparison in Table 6, whose earlier Figure 3b gives no run count, and ten seeds for DMLab. Mean plus/minus one standard deviation remains the convention. Some repeated Table 6 values match Table 1's five-seed results, leaving run provenance unclear; no increase in runs for retained experiments is established.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–3 and the original plotted results are retained, while substantial new results appear in the appendices. For example, Table 5 reports Sparse DMLab returns of 21.9 ± 2.6 for PGR(ECO) versus 16.3 ± 3.6 for PPO+ECO. New findings also cover noise robustness, exploration combinations, VAE underperformance, and refresh-frequency sensitivity. Some appendix rows reproduce earlier results.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds mathematical definitions of RND-, pseudo-count-, and episodic-curiosity relevance functions in Equations (6)–(8), extending v1's defined relevance functions. Existing assumptions and Equations (1)–(5) are retained. No new theorem, proof, or formal performance guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims about prioritized generative replay, sample efficiency, diversity, and scaling remain. However, the conclusion narrows curiosity from 'the right choice' to 'a good default choice,' and the introduction replaces reliable approximation with the ability to approximate the desired distribution. This modestly qualifies the recommendation's scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of noise robustness through weaker coupling to learned dynamics, compatibility with implicit exploration, diffusion's advantage over VAEs, and the refresh-frequency tradeoff. Appendix B explicitly limits exploration conclusions because DMC/Gym are poorly suited to studying exploration. Section 5.2 also shifts its sparse-reward explanation toward scarcity of decision-critical data.

D1.justification: v2 adds substantial implementation information: RND network dimensions, CTS image resizing and context bins, ECO parameters and architecture, noisy/bootstrapped-network integration, and VAE architecture. It also newly specifies the 0.1 intrinsic-reward weight for the existing exploration-bonus comparison and supplies a project-page address. These disclosures considerably expand reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Beyond the largely retained related-work section, Appendices A–C substantially expand positioning relative to intrinsic and episodic exploration, noisy/bootstrapped Q-learning, and model-based active exploration. New discussions explain compatibility with exploration methods and distinguish PGR from MAX and Dreamer-V3 through weaker dynamics coupling, accompanied by citations to the corresponding prior work.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact. v2 makes localized grammatical and wording edits, adds appendix pointers and funding acknowledgments, and organizes the added material into Appendices A–D. The additional scientific content does not amount to extensive rewriting of the original paper.

P2.justification: v2 adds dedicated comparison tables, noisy-DMLab example images in Figure 8, and the refresh-frequency plot in Figure 9. Table 9 visually distinguishes PER and VAE rows with color. Tables 6 and 9 partly redisplay earlier findings; the original figures and tables are retained with only small spacing and header changes.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for PGR's flexibility and applicability through alternative relevance functions, stochastic navigation, exploration combinations, and generator and robustness tests. It also qualifies curiosity as a default and acknowledges limits on exploration claims, addressing important questions left open in v1. Conflicting seed labels and Table 8's state/action-noise mismatch weaken reproducibility of some additions, but the broader validation and better-qualified interpretations provide a substantial net improvement.
